pack.name: EU GDPR — AI processing core
coverage: solely automated decisions, including the special-category restriction under Article 22
data protection by design and by default
known_gaps: This profile does not encode every GDPR duty, derogation or Member State provision.
Legal bases, transparency notices, processor terms, transfers, retention and data-subject rights require fuller profiles.
Article 22 and DPIA conclusions depend on legal interpretation and concrete effects.
pack.notice: This pack is an AI-oriented screening aid and not a complete record of processing activities or legal opinion.

fact_catalog.question: Is the decision based solely on automated processing?
Does the decision produce legal or similarly significant effects?
Is the decision necessary for entering into or performing a contract with the data subject?
Is the decision authorised by applicable Union or Member State law that also lays down suitable safeguards?
Has the data subject given valid explicit consent to this decision?
Is the solely automated decision based on special categories of personal data within Article 9(1)?
For this decision, is an Article 9(2)(a) or 9(2)(g) condition established as required by Article 22(4)?
Are applicable safeguards, including human intervention and contestation, implemented?
Is there systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects based on automated processing?
Are special-category or criminal-conviction data processed on a large scale?
Is there systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area on a large scale?
Has a suitable DPIA been completed before processing?
Are data-protection-by-design and default measures evidenced?

anchors.summary: Principles relating to processing of personal data and accountability.
Processing of special categories is prohibited unless a listed condition applies.
Right not to be subject to certain solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to conditions and safeguards.
Data protection by design and by default.
DPIA requirement for processing likely to result in high risk, with listed trigger categories.

rules.title: Personal data processing is in scope

finding.title: The described processing uses personal data
finding.summary: The GDPR profile applies; document purposes, roles, legal basis, data categories, recipients, retention, safeguards and rights.

obligations.title: Establish the full processing record and accountability evidence.

finding.title: No Article 9 condition is established
finding.summary: The processing uses special-category data but the inventory does not establish a permitted Article 9 condition.

obligations.title: Do not proceed until a valid Article 9 condition and safeguards are documented.

finding.title: Article 22 automated-decision safeguards must be resolved
finding.summary: The described decision is solely automated and has legal or similarly significant effects.

obligations.title: Establish whether an Article 22(2) condition permits the decision.
Where applicable, implement human intervention, expression of viewpoint and contestation safeguards.

finding.title: No Article 22(2) condition is established
finding.summary: The solely automated significant decision is not evidenced as contractually necessary, authorised by law or based on explicit consent.

obligations.title: Do not rely on the solely automated decision until an Article 22(2) condition is validly established.

finding.title: The permitted automated decision lacks evidenced safeguards
finding.summary: An Article 22 condition is asserted, but the applicable safeguards are not evidenced.

obligations.title: Implement and document the safeguards required for the relevant Article 22 condition.

finding.title: The special-category conditions for this automated decision are not established
finding.summary: A solely automated significant decision is based on special-category data, but the limited Article 9(2)(a) or 9(2)(g) condition and suitable safeguards required by Article 22(4) are not both evidenced.

obligations.title: Do not use special-category data for the decision until an Article 9(2)(a) or 9(2)(g) condition and suitable safeguards are established.

finding.title: A listed DPIA trigger is established
finding.summary: The supplied facts match at least one Article 35(3) trigger category.

obligations.title: Complete and document a DPIA before the processing starts; consult the authority where residual high risk remains.

rules.title: Required DPIA not evidenced as complete

finding.title: A required DPIA is not evidenced as complete
finding.summary: The processing matches a listed Article 35(3) trigger and the inventory does not evidence completion of a suitable DPIA before processing.

obligations.title: Complete and document the DPIA before processing and resolve any residual high risk through the applicable consultation process.

finding.title: Data-protection-by-design measures are not evidenced
finding.summary: Personal data are processed, but suitable design and default measures are not established in the inventory.

obligations.title: Define technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risks and processing context.
